text:
kiran: Heads-up — ACME (private/VPC) asked for a final hardware sizing for their Q4/autumn promo window. They want guidance by EOD tomorrow. Key constraints: air-gapped control plane, customer wants on-prem racks in 2 regions (primary+DR), limited egress (throttled NAT), and strict KMS integration. Current prod-like footprint they reported: ~30 steady requests/s, daily 12M tokens, avg req tokens ~140, tail peak bursts go to ~140 req/s for short windows (1–2h). Model target: 13B chat model quantized (FP16->int8 candidate). Can we sketch a minimal + recommended config and callouts?

mina: Quick take — we should dimension for 2-hour sustained peak with 25–30% headroom for safety. If bursts are longer we need pre-warmed instances or standing capacity. Air-gapped means slower patching and no live fallback to hosted, so redundancy is critical.

alec: Agree. Also watch NIC + PCIe topology — NVLink across GPUs matters for multi-GPU batching. If customer wants >1 model replica per node, prefer NVLink groups (DGX-style) or fat nodes (4–8 GPUs with NVSwitch).

jean: Doing a rough GPU-hours calc. If baseline is 30 req/s -> estimate tokens/s = 30 * 140 = 4200 tokens/s. Peak burst 140 req/s -> 19.6k tokens/s. Assume efficient batching + int8 -> throughput per H100-80GB single GPU ~6k tokens/s sustained for this model (conservative). So:
```
Baseline GPU need = ceil(4200 / 6000) = 1 GPU
Peak sustained (2h) = ceil(19600 / 6000) = 4 GPUs
Add 30% headroom -> 5 GPUs per region (primary), replicate DR = 5 (hot-warm?)
Estimated GPU-hours for 2 regions over peak day: 5 GPUs * 24h * 2 regions = 240 GPU-hours (but we can autoscale outside peak)
```
(very rough, we should run perf tests on quantized build)

kiran: Nice calc. A few questions: 1) Customer prefers A100 80GB or H100 — which is more cost-efficient for inference? 2) Do we recommend dedicated single-tenant racks or mixed tenancy? 3) Networking: NAT throughput and per-VM connection limits might throttle concurrency.

mina: For cost-efficiency: H100s win for larger models and mixed workloads (better tensor core perf), but A100 is still reasonable if they only run one quantized 13B. H100 gives higher perf/latency but is pricier per-hour. For sizing, present both: conservative (A100x4 per node) vs high-perf (H100x4).

alec: On tenancy — for customers with compliance, dedicated racks simplify audit and reduce noisy neighbor risk. But that increases cost. If they want predictable SLAs, recommend dedicated pool + a small shared warm pool for burst absorption (we can bill differently).

ops-lead: Networking note — customer NAT gateway is 25Gbps shared across VMs; with many TLS sessions we could saturate CPU on the gateway. Recommend: 25GbE with option for 100GbE uplinks for infra racks, and enable TCP offload on NAT appliance. Also add metrics to track socket_count and conn_rate.

sre-bot: Incident template created: private-vpc-q4-sizing-checklist-1778200123. Added items: KMS verification, air-gap upgrade plan, power/cooling check, rack PDU capacity, cross-region replication test.

jean: Also call out storage for KV cache. If they use local NVMe for prefix cache, add ~1–2TB per node depending on session retention. If they want long-lived chat sessions, we should size for cache objects: estimate 100k active sessions -> ~200–400GB cache.

mina: Ops suggestions to lower GPU count: 1) aggressive prefix caching to avoid re-tokenizing long histories, 2) dynamic sequence truncation based on prompt heuristics, 3) quantization to int8 with per-layer calibration. Together these can drop GPU time by ~30–50% in practice.

alec: Risk list for proposal — slow KMS responses add latency to startup, egress throttles prevent contacting monitoring endpoints (we need relay/batch agent), and air-gap means delayed security patches for CUDA/cuDNN which affects compatibility. We'll include fallback plan: add one smaller warm node in DR that can take <50% throughput if primary goes down.

kiran: Can someone produce a two-column recommendation (Minimal / Recommended) with explicit GPU counts, NIC, rack power, and cost ballpark for ACME? Minimal should assume no warm pool, Recommended includes warm pool + DR hot-warm strategy.

jean: I'll draft numbers and put in a short spreadsheet, but quick sketch here:
- Minimal: per-region: 3x A100-80GB (or 2x H100), 25GbE uplink, 1TB NVMe, 12kW rack PDU headroom. Single replica primary, cold DR (can spin up in ~30m).
- Recommended: per-region: 5x H100 (or 6x A100), 100GbE uplink, 2TB NVMe, redundant PDUs, hot-warm DR with 50% capacity, autoscale policy for bursts (pre-warm 2 GPUs 15m before predicted promos).

mina: Add budget note: H100 nodes ~+30–50% HW cost vs A100 but reduce required GPU count and give margin on latency SLO. For CAPEX customers, show 3-year TCO comparing both options including ops overhead for dedicated racks.

kiran: Perfect — thanks. Jean, can you post the spreadsheet link and a one-paragraph exec summary in thread before EOD? We'll use that for the customer call. Also include a 'must-test' perf matrix so ACME can validate the quantized model on their hardware.

jean: Will do — posting draft in ~2 hours. I'll include perf tests: 1) single-GPU 1-thread latency, 2) multi-GPU batching throughput sweep, 3) KMS failure mode, 4) NAT-limited long-tail test.

alec: And add recommended kernel flags and Docker runtime hints (MPS off for multi-tenancy, set CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES, disable GPU clock-persistence), plus notes on PCIe bifurcation if their boards are odd.

kiran: Great. If anyone has sample configs or previous customer numbers that map to these numbers, drop them here — especially any real-world H100 -> req/s numbers so Jean can tune the spreadsheet. :thumbsup:

mina: Pasting a tiny perf snippet we used internally on a quantized 13B (for reference):
```
# single H100-80GB, int8, batch=8 -> 7.2k tokens/s
# single A100-80GB, int8, batch=8 -> 4.8k tokens/s
# 4x H100 NVLink cluster with model-shard/batching -> ~25k tokens/s
```

sre-bot: Reminder: add runbook step for 'force-cooldown' if a node hits 95% GPU temp for >10m.

kiran: Thanks all — this is exactly what I needed. Jean/ Mina/Alec — loop back once the spreadsheet is up and we'll lock the proposal for ACME call tomorrow. :rocket:
